verses.text: Then we turned and headed up the road to Bashan. Og, the king of Bashan, came out with all his people to fight us at Edrei.
Yahweh told me, “Don’t be afraid of him. I’ve handed him over to you, along with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon.”
So Yahweh our God handed Og, the king of Bashan, and all his people over to us too. We struck them down and left no survivors.
At that time we took all his towns. We didn’t leave a single one untaken: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob in Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
Those towns were all fortified with high walls, gates, and bars. There were also a great many villages without walls.
We destroyed them completely, just as we did to Sihon, king of Heshbon. We destroyed every inhabited town, including the women and the little ones.
We kept all the livestock and everything we took from the towns as plunder for ourselves.
At that time we took the land from the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley all the way to Mount Hermon.
(The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites call it Senir.)
We took all the towns on the plain, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns in Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
(Og, king of Bashan, was the last one left of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron. Isn’t it still in Rabbah of the Ammonites? It was nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the standard cubit.)
Here’s how I divided the land we took then. I gave the Reubenites and Gadites the land from Aroer by the Arnon Valley, plus half the hill country of Gilead and its towns.
I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, Og’s kingdom, to the half-tribe of Manasseh. That included the whole region of Argob, all of Bashan. (It’s also known as the land of the Rephaim.
Jair son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob, right up to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He named those places in Bashan after himself, and they’re still called Havvoth Jair.)
I gave Gilead to Machir.
I gave the Reubenites and Gadites the land from Gilead to the Arnon Valley, with the middle of the valley as the border, and out to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
I also gave them the Arabah, with the Jordan as its border from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below the eastern slopes of Pisgah.
At that time I told you, “Yahweh your God has given you this land as your own. All your fighting men will cross over armed ahead of your fellow Israelites.
Your wives, children, and livestock will stay in the towns I gave you. I know you’ve got a lot of livestock.

Stay with your brothers until Yahweh gives them rest as he gave you rest, and they take possession of the land Yahweh your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you can go back to the land I gave you.”
At that time I told Joshua, “You saw with your own eyes what Yahweh your God did to these two kings. Yahweh will do the same to all the kingdoms you’re going to cross into.
Don’t be afraid of them. Yahweh your God himself fights for you.”
At that time I pleaded with God:
“Lord Yahweh, you’ve started to show your servant how great you are and how strong your hand is. What god in heaven or on earth can do the mighty things you do?
Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, that beautiful mountain and Lebanon.”
But Yahweh was angry with me because of you and wouldn’t listen. He told me, “Enough! Don’t bring this up with me again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah. Look west, north, south, and east, and see it for yourself. You won’t cross this Jordan.
Give Joshua his charge, encourage him, and make him strong. He’ll cross ahead of these people and lead them into the land you’re about to see, so it becomes their inheritance.”
So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.
